Ivano Iannelli
Sustainability Economics & Impact Measurement
Providing sustainability expertise, impact measurement frameworks and economic validation. Ivano helps organisations transform sustainability commitments into measurable commercial value.
ivano@EIG.com +971 50 558 7503 linkedin.com/in/thegreeneconomist

Ivano Iannelli is a development economist and internationally recognised authority on climate finance, carbon markets economics, and ESG governance, with 30+ years of experience advising governments, sovereign wealth funds, multilateral institutions, and publicly listed companies on the commercial and regulatory dimensions of the energy transition.

Current Role — CEO, TRST01 Climate Intelligence
Ivano serves as Chief Executive Officer of TRST01 Climate Intelligence, a DIFC-based Centre of Excellence deploying native agentic AI infrastructure for Paris Agreement compliance. TRST01 is currently operationalising World Bank-supported programmes in the DRC and Malawi, originating compliance carbon assets and ITMOs under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, and developing institutional-grade climate finance platforms for infrastructure-scale energy transition investments across emerging markets.

Emirates Global Aluminium — Senior Advisor to CEO
As Senior Advisor to the CEO of EGA, one of the world's largest industrial exporters to the EU and United States, Ivano led the pre-IPO sustainability transformation of a sovereign-linked, multi-billion-dollar operator — elevating EGA's Sustainalytics global ranking to 2nd worldwide, designing the CBAM compliance programme and a USD 250 million decarbonisation fund.

Dubai Carbon — CEO
Built one of the GCC's primary climate advisory and project development institutions under the Dubai Supreme Council of Energy. Contributed to national GHG inventories, NDC development, and structured the Dubai Green Fund — a sovereign investment vehicle mobilising private capital into sustainable infrastructure at scale.

United Nations — Chief of Programmes
Managed IFI-funded programmes across post-conflict environments in Africa and the Middle East, contributing to the development of CORSIA. Maintains active engagement with ICAO, IATA, the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market, and World Bank-led carbon pricing initiatives.

Education:
Doctorate (viva pending), Environmental Economics — Heriot-Watt University
MBA, Aviation Management — Coventry University
Executive Education, AI, Leadership & Innovation Strategy — Harvard Business School
"Sustainability is not a reporting function. It is the architecture of long-term competitive advantage — deeply rooted in strategy, not marketing."
Combined Experience
The future belongs to organisations that can understand complexity, create value and adapt with confidence.

EIG exists to help them do exactly that.

The EIG leadership team combines more than 100 years of real-world leadership experience across the disciplines that matter most to modern organisations.

We have led in government, healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, education, energy and economic development. We have designed and delivered transformation programmes, built AI and digital capabilities from the ground up, and created sustainability frameworks that deliver genuine commercial value.

What unites us is a shared commitment to one thing: creating measurable outcomes for the organisations and communities we serve.

We do not believe in consulting deliverables for their own sake. We believe in impact — real, verifiable, lasting impact that makes organisations stronger and more resilient.

Dr Patrick McCrudden
PhD — Global Value Chain & Supply Chain Strategy
Team@EIG.com LinkedIn

Dr Patrick McCrudden brings over three decades of hands-on global supply chain and logistics leadership to EIG, operating across some of the world's most demanding commercial and infrastructure environments. His career spans end-to-end supply chain management across multiple sectors and continents.

Career Highlights
Tesco — Regional Dairy Logistics, UK: Managing regional dairy logistics across the North West of England within a network of 400 dedicated farmers — developing the supply chain rigour and operational discipline that underpins his approach to complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Manila: Directing procurement and inbound logistics for the construction of a 7.25 MW dual-unit power station serving the airport complex — delivering a critical infrastructure programme on time and within budget across a complex multi-jurisdictional environment.
Johnson Electric, Hong Kong: Led a $1.2 million, six-month procurement and fit-out programme for 25,000 workers across 14 production buildings during the SARS crisis — delivering on time and within budget amid considerable operational uncertainty.
FirstNet, UK: Sourcing specialist IT infrastructure for UK-wide operational delivery — developing international vendor management capability across local, regional and global supply markets.
Franke — Walmart China Hyperstore Expansion: Managing stainless steel equipment supply chains and introducing process innovations that reduced commissioning timescales by over 50%.
Education & Qualifications
PhD, Global Supply Chain and Operations Management — University of Salford
MSc, Procurement, Logistics and Supply Chain Management
ISO 9001 Quality Management Auditor (Qualified)
HACCP Food Safety Manager (Certified)
At EIG

Patrick's role at EIG bridges global value chain strategy, procurement governance and operational delivery — ensuring that every engagement is supported by robust sourcing frameworks, international logistics intelligence and the supply chain rigour that protects client value at every stage of execution.

His experience spans Asia, the Philippines, Europe and the Middle East — from Fortune 500 procurement to airport infrastructure — making him uniquely positioned to advise on complex, multi-jurisdictional supply chain and procurement challenges.

"Supply chain rigour is not overhead. It is the architecture of operational resilience — and it is where the greatest difference between organisations that perform and organisations that struggle is most clearly visible."
